Characteristics of Postmodernism
Postmodernism in design is characterized by eclecticism, irony, and a disregard for traditional forms
Designers like Michael Graves playfully integrated classical elements with architectural structures,
creating visual experiences that are both whimsical and novel. Humor and historical references became
hallmarks of this period, blurring the lines between past and present.

New Wave Graphic Design
New Wave graphic design originated as a reaction
against the rigid grid structures of Swiss modernism
Designers broke conventions by incorporating layers and
rich visual references to create interactive and dynamic
visuals, making New Wave design more vibrant and
engaging. This style found widespread application in
advertisements, music posters, and mainstream media
enhancing audience interaction and visual engagement.

creative artworks, redefining the value of waste
